name: Should I convert a guest tub to a shower in a small bathroom?

mainEntity.name: Is it worth converting a guest bathtub to a shower in a small bathroom, or should I keep the tub?
mainEntity.text: Is it worth converting a guest bathtub to a shower in a small bathroom, or should I keep the tub?

acceptedAnswer.text: A tub-to-shower conversion can be a smart move in a guest bathroom when the room is tight and the goal is easier access, a cleaner look, and more usable shower space. It often works well in homes where the guest bath functions mostly as a daily secondary bath rather than a family bath. Keeping the tub makes sense if you want flexibility for children, plan to sell to a broader buyer pool, or want the bathroom to serve multiple age groups. In Los Angeles homes, the right answer often depends on square footage and the existing layout. A shower can feel more spacious, but a poorly planned conversion can create splash issues, awkward proportions, or drainage problems. The best conversions maintain comfortable clearances, proper waterproofing, and a shower design that fits the room instead of crowding it. If resale matters, think about the rest of the home and whether eliminating the tub reduces appeal in your market segment.
acceptedAnswer.description: A tub-to-shower conversion can make a small guest bathroom feel larger and more practical for adult guests. Keeping a tub may be better if the home serves children, resale is a priority, or you want a second bathing option. The best choice depends on how the bathroom is used and the room size.
